clue.text: Tiny shrill sound perhaps … Young birds (not large) in trees

indicators.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large, so saying 'not large' asks for that letter to be dropped

parts.note: wee is Scottish and informal British for small
a ping is one example of a high, sharp sound, hence 'perhaps'
Will Young is an English pop singer, winner of the first Pop Idol
owls are nocturnal birds of prey

explanation.surface: A tiny chirp heard from fledglings that are not large, hidden away in the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young birds' looks like chicks, but Young is the singer Will Young and the birds are OWLS losing their L. WEEPING and WILLOWS are built separately and simply set side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Weeping willows are a familiar variety of ornamental tree with drooping branches, often planted beside water.

clue.text: Dodgy régimes may produce these?

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable and not straight, so the letters that follow are not in their proper order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the accent

explanation.surface: Shady governments tend to drive people to flee the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: shuffled letters of the governments, and a description of what such governments cause. The accent on régimes hints at the French-flavoured answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Émigrés are people who have left their own country, typically for political reasons, exactly what oppressive rulers generate.

clue.text: Strength of spirit in demonstration

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the measure of alcohol content in a distilled drink
second meaning: evidence establishing that something is true

explanation.surface: Courage of character shown by someone in a protest or display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strength of spirit' reads as courage, but the spirit is liquor such as whisky or gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcoholic drinks are rated by their proof number, and a proof is also evidence that establishes a claim conclusively.

clue.text: Outstanding number at head of data collection

indicators.note: being at the head of something means coming first, so one piece is placed in front of the other

parts.note: NO is the standard abbreviation for number
a table is an arrangement of data in rows and columns

explanation.surface: An unpaid figure sits at the top of a spreadsheet of records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding number' suggests a debt still owed, but outstanding is the definition and number is just NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something outstanding stands out from the rest, deserving attention; remarkable and worthy are close synonyms.

clue.text: Who'll shortly send you to sleep?

definitions.text: Who'll shortly send you to sleep?

parts.words: Who'll shortly send you to sleep?
parts.note: surface reading: someone who will soon put you to sleep, like a sedative or a boring speaker
setter's reading: the nursery-rhyme figure is small, and he is the one who tells children to go to bed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' looks like 'soon', but it describes the character's small size. He is the nursery-rhyme boy who runs through the town in his nightgown checking that children are in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's little figure calls at windows ordering children off to bed, a personification of bedtime itself.

clue.text: Nestled among azalea, N.T. officer's shed?

indicators.note: a thing nestled among others sits snugly inside them, so the letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters across the end of the shrub and the initials

explanation.surface: A National Trust officer's garden hut tucked among the azalea bushes.
explanation.walkthrough: N.T. is the National Trust, the British charity that looks after historic houses and gardens; the abbreviation is there only to supply two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a small shed or outbuilding built against an existing wall, its roof sloping off that support.

clue.text: Bully proposers horribly

indicators.note: doing something horribly means doing it badly and messily, so the letters end up out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to intimidate people who put motions forward, and do it nastily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bully' reads as a verb, but it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An oppressor is someone who dominates and mistreats others with cruel power, which is what a bully does.

clue.text: Approves another helping

definitions.meaning: first meaning: formally supports a motion proposed by someone else
second meaning: a further portion of food at a meal

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests approving of somebody's assistance; the two halves are separate meanings, one from meetings and one from the dinner table.
explanation.definitionFit: In meetings one seconds a motion to back it, and at dinner asking for seconds means a further serving.

clue.text: Everyman, note, tucked into very old booze

indicators.note: something tucked into a space is placed inside it, so one pair of letters goes within the other

parts.note: V is the standard abbreviation for very
O is the standard abbreviation for old
the setter refers to himself, so 'Everyman' is me, I
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: The setter, with a memo, has hidden himself away among some ancient liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter naming himself, here Everyman, stands for I. The two-letter pair goes between the abbreviations V and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Vino is an informal word, borrowed from Italian, for wine, so it is a jokey term for alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Hollywood big shots actively kept a chart

indicators.note: acting actively means moving about energetically, so the letters are set in motion and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Film-industry moguls busily kept track of things on a graph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actively' reads as describing how they kept the chart, but it is the signal to rearrange the three words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rat Pack was the 1950s and 1960s group of famous entertainers, including Frank Sinatra and Dean Martin, who were film stars.

clue.text: Somewhat damp, ref abandons building

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, a part rather than the whole, so only a portion of the following letters is wanted

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the three words

explanation.surface: On a soggy pitch, the referee walks out and the match is called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandons' looks like a deletion instruction, and abandoned matches suit a wet pitch, but the answer simply runs through the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a prefabricated house, made in factory sections and assembled on site; Britain built many after the war.

clue.text: At last, interest and care shown adopting Pole

parts.note: INT is the standard abbreviation for interest, as on a bank statement

indicators.note: to adopt is to take someone into the family, so one piece takes another into itself

parts.note: to take heed is to take care
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: Finally, curiosity and kindness are shown in taking in a Polish child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a person from Poland, but it is a magnetic pole, North, giving N, which sits inside HEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean finally, after a long time or once everything has been taken into account.

clue.text: Surely sad? Sad, surely

indicators.note: sad in the slang sense of pathetic or in a sorry state, so these letters are in a poor condition and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a thing is really sad, then answers that it certainly is.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated words make it look like a riddle, but the first 'Surely' is the definition, the first 'sad' is the signal, and the last two words are the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adverbs expressing certainty or confidence, as in saying something will assuredly happen.

clue.text: Cushion on horseback, cowboy's accessory

parts.note: a rider who is mounted is said to be up
the leather case a cowboy wears to carry his gun

explanation.surface: A padded saddle pillow is part of a cowboy's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cushion' reads as a noun for a saddle pad, but it is a verb, to pad furniture. 'Up' for being on a horse is a racing usage: the jockey up is the one riding.
explanation.definitionFit: To upholster a chair or sofa is to fit it with padding, springs and fabric, making it soft and comfortable.

clue.text: Primarily, Antony's spouse's pets, sadly!

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of each word is taken

parts.note: the initial of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Sadly, the creatures Mark Antony's wife kept were the death of her.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Antony's spouse is Cleopatra, who killed herself with the bite of these snakes, hence 'sadly'.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend Cleopatra died by letting small venomous Egyptian snakes bite her, so they were her fatal companions.

clue.text: Ultimately stuck to bath oil that's in make-up bag

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the final letter of each word is taken

parts.note: the last letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Bath oil has stuck to something in a toiletry bag.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description of the thing rather than a synonym: something that's in a make-up bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Kohl is a black powder or pencil used as eyeliner, a cosmetic found among a person's beauty products.

clue.text: Specialised skill? Get to work in the allotment immediately, says Spooner

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds are exchanged

parts.words: Get to work in the allotment immediately
parts.note: to hoe is to weed a garden plot and now means at once; saying 'hoe now' with the opening sounds swapped

explanation.surface: Gardening know-how: someone urges you to start working your vegetable plot straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of 'hoe now' gives 'no how', spelt as two other words. An allotment is a small rented plot of land in Britain for growing vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Know-how is practical expertise, the specialised ability to do a particular task well.

clue.text: Mending and sorting washed socks?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: putting socks back in pairs after the wash

explanation.surface: A domestic chore list: darning holes and matching up the clean laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic, signalled by the question mark: read the word as RE-PAIRING, pairing again.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means restoring something to working order, and split differently it means matching items into pairs a second time.

clue.text: One loves seeing Star Wars villain, helmet removed, capturing space station

indicators.note: to capture is to hold prisoner, so one piece holds another inside it
a helmet sits on top of the head, so removing it takes off the first letter

parts.note: Darth Vader, the masked villain of the Star Wars films
Mir was the Soviet and then Russian space station in orbit from 1986 to 2001

explanation.surface: A fan watches Darth Vader take off his helmet and seize a space station.
explanation.walkthrough: Vader really does remove his helmet in the films, which makes the deletion look like plot; it strips the V, and the remainder splits around MIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An admirer is someone who loves or adores another, so 'one loves' describes the person doing the loving.

clue.text: Post-Christmas débris is irritating

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what a real Christmas tree sheds on the carpet in January
second meaning: provokes or annoys someone

explanation.surface: The mess left over after the festive season is annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs as one sentence, but it splits into a noun phrase and a verb phrase. The second definition must be read as a verb: it needles means it is irritating.
explanation.definitionFit: Pine trees drop their thin leaves as they dry out indoors, and to needle someone is to annoy them persistently.

clue.text: Wide-ranging, strove to secure a run

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast, so one piece holds the others within it

parts.note: vied means competed or strove to win
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A versatile batsman worked hard to get a single run on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: VIED splits after its first letter to hold the A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Something varied covers many different kinds of thing, so it is diverse and broad in scope.

clue.text: Word from above: disheartened Jewish scholar leaves

definitions.note: kohlrabi is grown mainly for its swollen stem, but it is a leafy green whose leaves are eaten too

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so losing heart means the middle letter is taken out

parts.note: the answer to 16 Across, which sits just above in the grid
a rabbi is a Jewish teacher of religious law

explanation.surface: A heavenly message reaches a dejected Jewish scholar, who then departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Word from above' sounds divine, but it means the grid entry above, 16 Across. 'Leaves' looks like the verb 'departs'; it is the vegetable's greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Kohlrabi is a cabbage-family vegetable, a type of leafy green with a bulbous stem, so it stands for edible foliage.

clue.text: In nobleman's house, outspoken style

indicators.note: outspoken literally means spoken out, so it is the word said out loud that counts

parts.note: a manor is the country house of a lord

explanation.surface: Inside an aristocrat's mansion, a blunt way of speaking is the fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outspoken' reads as frank, but it means said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A manner is a way or style of doing something, as in 'in the manner of' a particular artist.

clue.text: Absence of plonk nearly certain to end in failure

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter is left off

parts.note: plonk is cheap wine, so its absence is no wine

explanation.surface: A party with no cheap booze is bound to flop.
explanation.walkthrough: Plonk is British slang for cheap, ordinary wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-win situation is one where any course of action leads to a bad outcome, so it is doomed from the start.

clue.text: Tenth hiker represented in sculpture

indicators.note: to represent is to present again in another form, so the letters reappear rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The tenth walker in a group has been portrayed in a statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Represented in sculpture' reads as one phrase, but 'represented' is the signal and 'in' just joins it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodin's famous bronze of a seated man with chin on hand, lost in thought, is one of the world's best-known statues.

clue.text: Ably and supply

definitions.meaning: first meaning: competently, in a skilful way
second meaning: a source of water drawn from the ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ably and supply' looks like a rhyme with no picture; the two words are separate meanings. A well is a supply in the sense of a source, as in a well of information.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes doing something competently, and the noun is a shaft that provides water or oil.

clue.text: In war, new soldiers displayed malaise

indicators.note: things displayed are laid out and arranged for show, so the letters are set out in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fresh recruits sent into battle soon show signs of exhaustion and gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The war and soldiers set a scene of combat fatigue, which is close to the answer's meaning, but the fourteen letters are simply rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaise is a general feeling of unease or listlessness, and world-weariness is a jaded tiredness with life.
